claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies with sharp interphase boundaries.
Sharp interphase boundaries promote dislocation pile-ups in the starting alloy.
Dislocation pile-ups at the interphase boundaries cause local stress concentrations and premature microcracking.
A single brief sub-eutectic or intermediate-temperature post-solidification anneal is the proposed intervention.
The proposed anneal will promote nanoscale interdiffusion along the phase boundaries.
Annealing-induced interdiffusion will create diffuse, compositionally graded interfacial regions between the lamellae.
The graded interfaces will provide a more gradual mechanical-property transition between the lamellar phases.
A graded interface will soften the abrupt mechanical mismatch that otherwise drives dislocation accumulation.
The graded interface will enable more gradual accommodation of dislocations and reduce pile-up intensity.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups will lower local stress concentrations and delay microcrack initiation.
The annealed alloy will exhibit greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will maintain or slightly increase its yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The annealed alloy will undergo more homogeneous plastic deformation at room temperature.
The proposed improvement applies under room-temperature tensile loading at standard loading rates.
Excessive annealing time or temperature may cause over-diffusion or microstructural coarsening.
Over-diffusion or coarsening may diminish strengthening from the dual-phase microstructure.
A ductility improvement greater than 15% while retaining or enhancing strength is the specified experimental success criterion.
